Version history: everything built so far.

Version 0.0.1, pre-alpha, not yet published. 118 changes from 2026-10-17 to 2026-10-18, newest first, each with the commit and files it lives in. Changes marked "Being tested" are built but not yet proven on real devices.

Coming next

Planned or being tested, not finished. No dates are promised.

  • The Mac and Linux installers were built automatically but have not yet been installed and checked on real computers, so they are still being tested.

  • Public downloads and the source code have not been published yet; both are planned for the public beta.

    b496a2b; docs/spikes/S1-mobile-audio-and-inference.md ('Status: designed, not started'); apps/ contains only desktop and fixtures-v1

  • A single visit could not yet be deleted from inside the app, and an option to remove old recordings automatically after a set time was still planned.

    b496a2b; docs/plans/M0.md decision 8 (optional auto-delete policy); engine/os-app/src/lib.rs (only a failed import's folder is removed, no delete-visit command); apps/desktop/src/engine.ts

    a06874e; docs/plans/M2.md item 7 ('Not started'); no chart component in apps/desktop/src (Triadan appears only as a heading example)

  • Summaries of a patient's past records, including scanned PDFs read on the clinic's own computer, were planned but not started.

    a06874e; docs/plans/M2.md item 8 ('Not started') and 'Decisions for the product owner' (OCR engine still to choose); no OCR library in the engine

  • OpenBark has only been measured on synthetic test consults on one Windows computer; checking it in real clinics comes before any clinical use.

    7728e07; README.md (Status: 'has not yet been validated in real clinics'); docs/perf/M0.md; packages/eval/fixtures/

Clearer drafting progress and better-grounded notes

Transcription and drafting now show each step as it happens, and notes are written in the template's own heading order, which cut unsupported wording in testing.

  • Transcription shows a step-by-step board, from reading the recording to transcribing, checking numbers and saving, with elapsed time, an estimate and screen reader announcements.

    b468dc4; apps/desktop/src/components/ProgressBoard.tsx; apps/desktop/src/components/ProcessingBar.tsx

  • Drafting shows each heading of the template ticking off as the model writes it, followed by a check of every number against the transcript.

    b468dc4; apps/desktop/src/components/DraftProgress.tsx; engine/os-app/src/lib.rs

  • Redrafts and Reprocess keep the current note visible, dimmed, while the new draft is written, and multi-pet visits show which animal is being drafted.

    b468dc4; apps/desktop/src/screens/Review.tsx; apps/desktop/src/components/DraftProgress.tsx

  • Notes are now written in the template's heading order, history and exam before assessment, instead of alphabetically with Assessment first and Subjective last.

    b468dc4; engine/os-engine/src/template.rs; docs/eval/heading-order.md

  • On 13 synthetic test consults, wording not supported by the cited transcript lines halved, from 45 to 23, and wrong citations fell from 12 to 3.

    b468dc4; docs/eval/heading-order.md

  • In the same test, facts captured stayed level at 141 of 155 against 143 before, and invented numbers stayed at zero in both versions.

    b468dc4; docs/eval/heading-order.md

Consent, encryption and team members

Finished on 18 October: recording consent, encryption of every encounter file on disk, and team members with roles recorded against every change to a note.

  • A consent step before recording captured how the client agreed and who confirmed it, and saved this with the encounter.

    84f000c; apps/desktop/src/components/ConsentStep.tsx; engine/os-engine/src/session.rs

    5e357a6; docs/adr/0008-encryption-at-rest.md; engine/os-engine/src/vault.rs

2026-10-17

More accurate notes, with visible checks

A scoring tool for synthetic consults guided changes that raised accuracy, added a second listen for numbers and drug names, and gave every encounter patient details.

  • A new evaluation tool scores each draft against the known facts of synthetic consults, counting missed vitals and medications, invented numbers and citation errors.

    591ad1b; engine/os-cli/src/eval.rs; docs/eval/M1.md

  • Misheard drug and disease names, such as "marapitin" for maropitant, now get a visible suggestion on the transcript, and the transcript text itself is never changed.

    591ad1b; engine/os-engine/src/vocab.rs; packages/vocab/veterinary.tsv

  • Clinics can add their own words to the veterinary vocabulary these suggestions draw on, by editing a word list file on the computer.

    591ad1b; engine/os-engine/src/vocab.rs; docs/eval/M1.md

  • Measurements are now written as a number with a separate unit, and every vital in the synthetic tests came out correct with its unit.

    591ad1b; docs/eval/M1.md

  • A second speech recogniser, Whisper, listens again to lines with numbers or clinical terms and flags disagreements, such as 100 mL heard as 10 mL.

    837f400; engine/os-engine/src/crosscheck.rs; docs/eval/M1.md

  • Patient name, last name and reason for visit can be entered on the Recorder, edited on Review, and appear in Encounters and at the top of copied notes.

    837f400; apps/desktop/src/components/PatientFields.tsx; engine/os-engine/src/session.rs

2026-10-17

A plan and an engine that drafts SOAP notes

We set out the first milestone and built the local engine that turns a consult recording into a transcript and a cited SOAP draft.

  • We published the first milestone plan, chose the name OpenBark and released the code under the Apache-2.0 open-source licence.

    bb8ae01; docs/plans/M0.md, LICENSE, NOTICE

  • A consult recording became a transcript on the computer itself, using the Parakeet speech model, with no cloud service involved.
